does: Decides whether a character that joins a fight was surprised by an attack from hiding. It asks for a live hit whose target is that character, made from hiding (the attack flag FromSneak), by a spell that may surprise (its prototype lacks the spell flag NoSurprise), from an attacker that is not the character's ally; with such a hit the character is marked, and the combat system's update gives it esv::combat::SurprisedStealthRequestOneFrameComponent. FromSneak is bit 4 of the byte at +0x58 of eoc::hit::TargetComponent, NoSurprise bit 24 of the prototype's flags, an ally a relation of 100, and the mark the update state's set at +0x208.

evidence.says: the Toolkit's EoCServer.dll exports esv::combat::System::CheckForSurprise with the same body: the two queries (hit target with hit meta, hit attacker with hit meta), the same flag tests, the same set at +0x208

the first query is registered with eoc::hit::TargetComponent and eoc::hit::MetaComponent, the second with eoc::hit::AttackerComponent and eoc::hit::MetaComponent; the function returns at once for an entity without esv::Character; its only callers are three places of the start of a fight, one for each side of a pair of which at least one was in no fight

a count-only probe during a hidden archer's shot at one of two idle hostile humans shows 3 calls, one for each of the three that join the fight; the target alone gets the stealth request, in the tick it joins; with the targets already in a fight the same shot gives no request
